precepts.text: In whom all the building fitly framed together (that is you and me) groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord. You know what fitly framed together means? Stones have to come together. Brothers, we must merge together: whatever your position is, play that position; do not try to change positions through deceit. In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.
precepts.point: Frederick Douglass said, it is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men. All of us come in broken, broken with sins. So in order for us to grow mentally and spiritually and improve our character: verse one, lay it all aside, then desire the sincere milk of the word.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us. Peter says “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house”, and Paul shows how that house grows: “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”. All the building is you and me. See that word growing: Peter just explained how we grow, by laying aside all malice, all guile, all hypocrisies, all evil speakings, and desiring the sincere milk of the word.

You know what fitly framed together means? Stones have to come together. Brothers, we must merge together. Whatever your position is, play that position. Don't try to change positions through deceit. A brother was demoted in New York for lying over a simple thing; when we ask, most of the time we already know the answer, and when the witnesses are called, the liar is put on front street and found not worthy of his rank. A stone full of guile does not fit in the frame.

“In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.” Wherever our congregation is, that is a spiritual house, the real temple, and God dwells in it through the Spirit. That is why Zerubbabel is our example: he got to his position not only for his fighting skills but because he was of noble character, understanding God's truth. We should not be deceitful, envious, hateful or filled with guile toward one another, but lively stones with zeal, passion and fire, built together into the house where God lives.

precepts.text: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves; our communications must change.
precepts.point: Frederick Douglass said, it is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men. All of us come in broken, broken with sins. So in order for us to grow mentally and spiritually and improve our character: verse one, lay it all aside, then desire the sincere milk of the word.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
“Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” We are the temple, the spiritual house Peter speaks of. “If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves. Our communications must change. The malice, guile, hypocrisies, envies and evil speakings of 1 Peter 2:1 defile the temple.

Paul goes on in 2 Timothy: “Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation. There are brothers and sisters who are gold and silver, applying 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are those of wood and earth, meaning no good: fringes and a border of blue, but they have not changed their lives in two or three years. Not the new people, but those who have been with us for years and are still grimy, still that secret adulterer, still that liar, complainer, murmurer.

The captains must be able to identify in their school who is honourable and who is dishonourable. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge means cut them off, like pruning a plant and taking away the bad elements. I knew which brothers always got me in trouble; I almost got arrested many a time with those grimy brothers, and I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership. Keep the temple holy.

precepts.text: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. If you apply these two verses, everyone will see a substantial change in your life. But if you are the same grimy brother or sister from last year to the year before that, we know you have not been applying 1 Peter 2:1-2.
precepts.point: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto. Blessed are the peacemakers, but peace does not always work with some people; some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don't want peace with you.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Onias went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private.” Simon was full of malice, envy and evil speaking. Peter tells us what to do with all of that.

“Wherefore laying aside all malice”: when you give yourself to the Lord, one of the first things you must do in repenting is lay aside all malice. “And all guile”: guile means deceit; put it away from you. “And hypocrisies”: don’t be a hypocrite. “And envies”: whatever envies, hatreds and jealousies you have, put them from you. “And all evil speakings.”

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” You cast those sins away and start all over again as newborn babes, desiring the commandments in Christ. That is the only way you can grow in this truth.

If you apply verses 1 and 2, everyone will see a substantial change in your life. But if you are the same grimy brother or sister from last year and the year before that, we know you have not been applying 1 Peter 2:1-2. Our people forget history quickly; we cannot afford to become Simon.

precepts.text: Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation. Our people living like Gentiles will repent based on your conduct out there in the world.
precepts.point: Not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man, because Onias had a good report even among the other nations. The king was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead; and being kindled with anger, he took away Andronicus his purple, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city unto that very place where he had committed impiety against Onias, and there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.”

They may speak against us as evildoers, but they shall behold our good works. Why would they glorify God? Because our people who are living like Gentiles will repent based on your conduct out there in the world.

That is the lesson of Onias in 2 Maccabees 4. His conduct was honest before the nations, and even the Greeks and the king wept for him. Menelaus and Andronicus dealt in flattery, theft and deceit, and they brought reproach. Our conversation outside this truth is how our own people living like Gentiles will see it and come to repentance.

precepts.text: Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: as a believer in Christ you must follow the steps of Christ. Christ came to bring peace; bitterness does not do that.
precepts.point: But with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth: meaning, I have got the bitter spirit; I have to talk to my brother in sincerity and truth. You have to go to your brother.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. What is the example that Christ left? Peter: “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps”.

Christ suffered for us: that goes back to him being our Passover, sacrificed for us. And he left an example, so as believers in Christ we must follow his steps. Christ came to bring peace. Bitterness does not do that.

So we apply the scriptures. Purge out the old sin, the old man, that we may be a new lump, a new creature in Christ, following in the steps of Christ. “Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness”. That malice is the bitterness: a dumb thought jumps in, the seed gets planted, it gets nourished, and next thing you know you have malice, hatred toward your brother, and wickedness, because it leads to sin.

“but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth”. Meaning: I have the bitter spirit, so I have to go to my brother and talk to him in sincerity and truth. Brothers sweep under the floor mats and dump out the toaster at Passover, and there is not a grain of yeast in the house, while they carry an evil eye toward a brother or bitterness toward a wife. We are the temple of God; the leaven has to come out of the spirit.

And do not tuck it away for later, like the brother who puts the bread in the storage closet during the feast and brings it back when the season is over. Following Christ's steps means letting the bitterness go entirely.

precepts.text: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile: that is the fake talk because you are bitter; and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.
precepts.point: And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Peter shows what the renewing of the mind looks like: “Wherefore laying aside all malice.” Lay aside all malice, family: all malice, all leaven. “and all guile”: that is the fake talk, because you are bitter. “and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.” We have to lay these things aside.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” We have to be born again in Christ like newborn babes. The sincere milk of the word is the thing we have to desire, and it is what makes us grow.

This is Romans 12:2 at work. Being conformed to this world is carrying the mind of Cain and Esau: the malice, the guile, the envy and the evil speaking of the bitter spirit. Being transformed is laying all of that aside and feeding on the word until the mind is renewed after Christ.

precepts.text: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word. Christ's teeth were white with milk because he came teaching the laws.
precepts.point: Reading shown: contrary to common belief, European slave traders were fairly well informed about various African ethnicities, leading to slavers targeting certain ethnic groups which plantation owners preferred, so that desired ethnic groups became fairly concentrated in certain parts of the Americas. The slave traders knew which tribes they were transporting and where they put them. Even if you are light skinned, the curses fit you; you are an Israelite.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

precepts.why:
Genesis 49:12 says of Judah’s promised ruler, “his teeth white with milk.” The question is what the milk represents, and Peter answers it: “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” The milk is the word.

So Christ’s teeth were white with milk because he came teaching the laws. What came out of his mouth was the word, the laws of his Father. That is what the white like milk represents.

It is the same kind of speech as “his voice as the sound of many waters.” He had a deep voice, and the scripture says it the way our people talk, in idiom. When a king was rich the scripture says he waxed fat; when Saul relieved himself it says he covered his feet. That is hip talk, and it is how you know the scriptures were written by our people, Israelites who speak in parables, as Christ and the prophets did.

Read that way, the whole picture in Revelation lines up: a black man with woolly hair, like the woolly hair of the negro, white like wool, eyes red with wine, feet “like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace,” black like brass that has been burned, and a mouth full of the law.

precepts.text: Abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul: pornography is not normal, it means fornication, and it is a war for your soul, from the magazines in the ceiling to easy access today.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”. When you keep entertaining that sin, eventually you will be bound by it. Peter says, “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”.

This is a spiritual war, a war for your soul. Take porn. Brothers say, I got it under control; it don't bother me. No, you don't have it under control. Picture a hallway of doors. A lot of you say, I only watch straight porn, like it is a good thing. That is door number one. Then the threesome, then the train. After a while you get desensitized; that does not excite you anymore, so you go to the next door down: chicks with dicks, then bestiality, then scat, then lesbian, then pedophilia. That is where the doors lead.

It is not normal. And you know it is the devil: when the Bishop was a little kid, his father had magazines hidden up in the drop ceiling. How did two little boys know to get a chair and climb up there, when they never saw their father do it? Playboy, Hustler, then VHS, then DVDs, and today easy access in your hand.

That is how iniquity lifts itself up until you are bound with your sins, covered like a field with thorns. Abstain from fleshly lusts; they are at war with your soul.

precepts.text: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, by whose stripes ye were healed: how the Lord restores health.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
How does the Lord restore health unto us? “Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.”

Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. We, being dead to sin, should live unto righteousness. We are healed by Christ's punishment, his crucifixion.

That is the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:17: “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. How? When he sent Christ to die on the cross. By his stripes we are healed.

Then: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”. Outcast means African-American: made-up names they gave our race. Nobody gives a damn about you, blacks and Latinos; no man seeks after you. But the Lord does. The wound no medicine could close is healed by his stripes, and then “all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: every one of them, not some.

precepts.text: The whole creature was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them. The fringes, the beard, and the Sabbath are what separate you, and they were given only to us.
precepts.point: You were called out of darkness to show forth his praise. Nobody puts a light under a bushel. You shine from the front, so it is time to take your places.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Peter calls us “a peculiar people”. What makes us peculiar? Wisdom answers: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them”. The peculiar commandments, the same thing Deuteronomy 4 said, are what separate us. They see the fringes on your garment. They see a beard on your face. They ask why y'all never come out with us on Saturday, and you say I have to keep the Sabbath. The Sabbath, what's that? I thought you said you was Christian. That is what separates you from everybody else.

The commandments “that were given unto them”: all these things were given only to us. That is why 1 Peter 2:9 is talking about the Israelites, not the white man. It is not white Grecians in togas, and the Galatians are not the white man in Turkmenistan. It is talking about you. So many of our brothers and sisters have been destroyed and don't see themselves as a prince, a ruler, a judge, but God says you are all of those things. All the leadership books go back to the Bible, which was given only to us, yet they make billions off leadership conferences while we sit at the bottom.

We must magnify the law: “The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law”. That is each and every one of our jobs, to put the laws of God on a pedestal and stand firm for them. When you do, it automatically puts you in a different position, different from everybody else on the face of the earth, because nobody else is standing firm for the commandments. The way you do anything is the way you do everything; nine times out of ten the cracker over you on the job is no better than you, but you are not doing things according to the commandments.

That separation shows. Our sisters dress modestly while the women in Houston dressed so out of order a dress code had to be put in place. Fifty men reading the Bible on a cruise become the disturbance. They make a man an offender for the word. But we were called out of darkness to show forth his praise. Nobody takes a light and puts it under a bushel, and you don't shine from the back. It is time for all of us to take our places.

precepts.text: I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection, lest when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. You can control your sexual appetite by controlling your food intake: abstain from the foods you desire and are tempted with. Alcohol is stored in your brain with late nights and social gatherings, so refuse to drink in that environment and you tell your reward vectors who is in charge. Abstain from the candy you love, and you gain power over the things with more control over you. Then disconnect the feelings associated with pornography, Instagram, and looking, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a new habit, open a Bible instead, so the brain associates that environment with the new function.
precepts.point: I realized I actually have a lust for food: the jelly donut at Dunkin', the Doritos, thoughts replaying something you desire but are not supposed to have, until you justify one cookie and give in. That is no different from pornography, adultery, or fornication. And it is a big deal, because if you are not in the green you cannot go on the street; the Lord is putting a cap on us to show it is the exact same battle, a worldly lust inherited through America.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

precepts.text: Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth. A pastor claiming Christ was wrong for most of his life is the blind watchman in action.
precepts.point: Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber; greedy dogs which can never have enough. One locked the church doors until he got his forty thousand, another promised millionaires overnight for a ten-thousand-dollar seed. All prosperity, no prophecy.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark.” We are supposed to watch and pray, to be alert to the times, to keep our spirit in order with the Most High and to repent. But the watchmen are blind. All these Christian apologists and Black pastors are ignorant. We are on the brink of civil war in America, and how many pastors are saying prepare ye war? None of them. They are celebrating Valentine's Day. They cannot bark: they will not prophesy and they will not warn you, like the dog that jumped out the window when its own owner pretended to break into the house.

They are “sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber”, silent and lazy, and “greedy dogs which can never have enough.” One pastor said nobody leaves until he gets his 40 G's, lock the doors. Another said sow a seed of ten thousand and you'll be a millionaire overnight. All they speak about is prosperity: nothing about prophecy, nothing about warning you, nothing about getting your spirit right. Many don't even think they have a reason to bark, because they are too comfortable to see the danger right in front of them.

Here is one of the watchmen in action. Jamal Bryant, senior pastor of New Birth Missionary Baptist Church, preached with conviction that 85% of Jesus's life he was wrong and out of order, doing what he was not called to do, and the people sat there and listened to it.

The Bible says sin is the transgression of the law, the breaking and violating of God's laws. So was Christ wrong? Peter answers: “Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.” He did no wrong at all.

Yet a pastor will get up and speak against Christ, and you never hear him speak against Babylon, America, never against homosexuality, never against the idolatrous festivals out here. That is the blind watchman, the dumb dog that cannot bark. So the prophets have to go out and proclaim among the Gentiles, “Prepare war”, and our own people need to know war is coming too.

precepts.text: I will sow her unto me in the earth, and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy, and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God, which had not obtained mercy but now have obtained mercy. Peter is quoting Hosea 2:23 about the northern kingdom.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall hear Jezreel.” Jezreel is the seed of Israel. This is chapter 2 of the same context as Hosea 1:10-11, read earlier, where God gathers them together again and they appoint themselves one head.

“And I will sow her unto me in the earth”: I will bring her, adopt her back unto me in the earth. Then, “and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” Which were not my people, or not a people. That promise was made to the northern kingdom, in Isaiah 7 and 8 and in Hosea 1.

Now go back to Peter. He is writing to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia and the rest, the elect according to the foreknowledge of God, and he says “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” Sound familiar? Peter is quoting Hosea. When Christ dies he redeems them back into being his people and gathers them together in one.

The builders who stumbled were appointed to it: by rejecting Christ they had him killed, and by his being killed the northern kingdom was granted a chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold. Israelites that are not studying never see this. How could you find that out if you don't know your history?

precepts.text: Abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul, including lust for food.
precepts.point: Stop overeating and snacking, fast more, exercise, and ask the Lord never to remove that spirit of discipline.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.” If you are deceitful, that holy spirit of discipline is not going to live with you, and it will not stick around when you are in sin.

Peter names the war: “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”. That includes the lust for food. Overeating and snacking is a fleshly lust warring against your soul, and it drives out the spirit of discipline.

Thoughts “without understanding” are not knowing that we need you to do the work, so we need you healthy; your kids need you and you need yourself. So stop hating yourself and become disciplined. Fix your mind first and don’t say I can’t. Stop overeating, stop snacking, start fasting more, drink water instead of soda and juice, make exercise a lifestyle, eat light, and take care of your body.

Pray and fast that the Lord keeps your discipline. Ask him to change your appetite and strip away the cravings for sugar and processed carbs, and ask the Lord never to remove his holy spirit from you, so you can stay disciplined.

precepts.text: To the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God.
precepts.point: Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”, and verse 2 calls them “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ”. These strangers are the same strangers that came to keep the Passover in Chronicles, and the elect is the same name given to those called according to Hosea and Isaiah in Romans 9. Who's that? Israel.

So when verse 9 says “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, the “ye” is these same strangers scattered abroad. They are set against “them which be disobedient”: the builders that disallowed the stone, the southern kingdom, the Pharisees that rejected Christ and stumbled at that stone of stumbling and rock of offence of Isaiah 8:14. They were “appointed” to it. They had to put Christ to death, and his death gave the other kingdom the chance to repent and come back into the fold. By rejecting Christ they brought back in the same brothers they rejected.

The scattered elect were called “out of darkness into his marvellous light”, which is Isaiah 9:1. And they are the ones “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” That goes back to Deuteronomy 32 and Isaiah 7, not a people. The northern tribes, cast off and scattered, are now the people of God.

precepts.text: Servants, be subject to your masters, not only to the good and gentle.
precepts.point: Onesimus was a servant who fled Philemon, and Paul sent him back as a brother.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” This is in the slave Bible; Esau used it. But the good and gentle masters and the froward ones were Israelite masters. The law said not to deal with Israel with rigour, meaning hard, yet some of them were like that. The froward ones are the ones who did not really like you.

“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

Why would a master not like his servant? Exodus 22: a thief found breaking in, “If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” That is different from a poor brother saying, I lack food, clothing and shelter, will you help me? If I broke into your house, stole all your stuff and got caught, now I have to work for you, and you are not going to like me too much. You have to see him every morning.

So Peter tells servants to be subject even to the froward master, and to take it patiently. It is Israelite servitude under the law, not chattel slavery.

precepts.text: Christ suffered for us, who did no sin; no blemish means no sin, the one flawless sacrifice.
precepts.point: That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
“Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth”.

Without blemish physically was symbolic of no sin. The bruise, the cut, the stain that disqualified an animal stood for sin, and Christ had none of it: he was the one and only flawless sacrifice. That is why the peace offering had to be without blemish before the Lord.

precepts.text: Enduring grief, suffering wrongfully, is thankworthy; that is what Christ went through for us, and the pattern for us when we suffer for well doing.
precepts.point: That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
Christ also suffered wrongfully, and that is thankworthy with God: “this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.”

“For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.” That is what Christ went through for us, and it is the pattern for us: when you follow his steps and suffer wrongfully without adding a blot to your honor, that is acceptable with God, the way the offering without blemish was acceptable.

precepts.text: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby; the milk is the first five books.
precepts.point: Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. The milk is the dos and the don’ts, the first five books.

Many want to run to Revelation and the parables, but the solutions for what is wrong in your spirit, for lust, covetousness, hatred, malice, and envy, sit in the ordinances and the commandments. Look up the scriptures on patience, temperance, and how to treat your family correctly. That is how a soul stops trespassing against the Lord through ignorance.

precepts.text: Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.
precepts.point: The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
The sin offering is most holy, and Christ was the sin offering, most holy. “Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth”. Guile is deceit, and none was found in his mouth.

“Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously”. He left us an example that we should follow his steps; if you do not keep the commandments of God you are not following his steps.

precepts.text: Christ left us an example that we should follow his steps; the steps are commandment keeping.
precepts.point: Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Phinehas received the covenant of peace and the everlasting priesthood “because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.” Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions.

“For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps.” Christ suffered for us and left us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God.

The first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

precepts.text: A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people: Peter and Moses speak the same thing about the same people.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”. Peter and Moses speak the same thing about the same people.

Peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group or thing, and different from the usual or normal. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: the Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. That is “your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations”.

Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ. But rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Keep the statutes and judgments, and the nations see a royal priesthood, an holy nation, and say “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”

precepts.text: Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; the same title as Deuteronomy 14:2.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” Peter writes to that same peculiar people: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”.

It is the same title Moses gave Israel: an holy nation, a peculiar people. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and Peter's letter is addressed to them, the strangers scattered through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

That is what is taught to our people today: raising them back up into the understanding of who they are, and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

precepts.text: A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a peculiar people, which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
Peter writes to that peculiar people: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”. The peculiar people the Lord avouched here is the peculiar people Peter writes to. We were called out of our sins into the light, and the light is the commandments and the law.

“Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” We were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro; but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel, the people of God.

precepts.text: This is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully; but examine yourself before you use this precept to play the victim, for the Lord knows what is behind closed doors.
precepts.point: Give place to the law of the Most High: whatever situation you are going through, the solution is in the Bible, so do not let anger close the book on you. Sometimes the answer is to suffer wrongfully, and what matters is not who is right but what the right thing to do is according to the Bible.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.” Sometimes the answer is to suffer wrongfully. What matters is not who is right but what the right thing to do is according to the Bible.

But examine yourself before you use this precept to play the victim, for the Lord knows what is behind closed doors. Give place to the law of the Most High; the solution to whatever you are going through is in the Bible.

precepts.text: With well doing ye put to silence the ignorance of foolish men; David kept behaving wisely and left Saul nothing to charge him with.
precepts.point: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them; everybody knew he was the one really putting his life on the line and doing the work, even though he had no throne.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
“For so is the will of God, that with well doing ye may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men.” David kept behaving wisely and left Saul nothing to charge him with.

And the people saw it: “all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.” Everybody knew he was the one really putting his life on the line and doing the work, even though he had no throne.

precepts.text: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the froward, to those that are like Nabal; enduring grief wrongfully for conscience toward God is thankworthy.
precepts.point: She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do; instead she pleaded, Let not my lord regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. She had not seen the young men David sent, or she would have stepped in then to protect their house.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” The froward are those that are like Nabal. “For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.”

Abigail fell at David's feet and said, “Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be.” She was not the one who did anything wrong, but she took that iniquity upon herself. She was being that pillar of her house, using wisdom to protect it, for the scripture says she was a woman of good understanding.

She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do. She pleaded, “Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I thine handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.” Had she seen them, she would have stepped in then to protect their house.

precepts.text: If ye take it patiently when ye do well and suffer for it, this is acceptable with God.
precepts.point: Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

precepts.why:
“For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

What came on David from Absalom and Ahithophel came for his own faults, as the Most High spoke in chapter 12; none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. There is no glory in being buffeted for your faults. The suffering that is acceptable with God is to do well, suffer for it, and take it patiently.

precepts.text: As newborn babes desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow thereby.
precepts.point: We have to come back to this Bible as a child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why: “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. David behaves and quiets himself, calming himself as a child weaned of his mother. Coming into the truth we must desire the sincere milk of the word, the basics, and grow from there.

precepts.text: As newborn babes we are to desire the sincere milk of the word, the easy things to be understood, that we may grow thereby.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. The new convert is a newborn babe, and the sincere milk of the word is the easy things to be understood: keeping the laws, not harboring hatred, taking care of one another, being charitable and forgiving.

That is what the little sister with no breasts must desire, that she may grow thereby, until her breasts are like towers and she is found with favour in his eyes.

precepts.text: We as lively stones are built up a spiritual house; this spiritual house represents Israel.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.” We, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house. That spiritual house represents Israel.

So the house whose threshold the waters come from under, whose forefront stands toward the east, is the house of Israel, not a literal building. Ezekiel speaks by similitude and dark sayings, and the waters coming down from under the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar, are the word of the Most High issuing out.

precepts.text: A chosen generation, a holy nation, which in time past were not a people but now are the people of God, having obtained mercy.
precepts.point: The restoration is two sticks made one nation. Ephraim, once "not a people," is called back and named the sons of the living God, having obtained mercy that they had not obtained, so the Gentiles being brought in are the outcasts of Israel that Christ came to be a light to.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Peter himself wrote it: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.”

That is Hosea's word to Ephraim, word for word in meaning: not a people, now the people of God; had not obtained mercy, now have obtained mercy. The Gentiles being brought in are the northern kingdom, and Peter, who once said he would not keep company with one of another nation, wrote to them as a holy nation.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
When Paul came to Jerusalem the apostles perceived the Most High was dealing with him based on his ministry and the people he was waking up. You can tell the spirit on someone by how they move. Peter writes to those same people: “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.”

If the spirit of the Most High is in you, it compels you to keep pushing forward in the truth no matter how tired or exhausted, a lively stone built into the spiritual house. Those who are faking it can only do it for so long before they pull back, become less visible, and eventually leave.
